# worker-sync-db

> Offline-first IndexedDB for browser SPAs: SharedWorker multi-tab live updates and bring-your-own (BYO) sync to your API. TypeScript core; optional React hooks. Not a sync SaaS.

npm: `worker-sync-db` · MIT · browser-only (needs `window`)

## When to use

- Web app must work offline and catch up when online
- Multiple tabs should show the same data without custom BroadcastChannel glue
- You want IndexedDB + TypeScript and **your** push/pull backend (not Dexie Cloud / Firebase lock-in)
- Optional React live queries (`worker-sync-db/react`)

## When not to use

- Server-side / Node storage (this is browser IndexedDB only)
- You need CRDTs or complex conflict resolution (v1 is last-write-wins on timestamps)
- Single-tab CRUD with no multi-tab or BYO sync needs — Dexie or raw `idb` may be simpler
- Safari-first multi-tab sync (SharedWorker missing; `mode: 'auto'` falls back to dedicated, no cross-tab)

## Install

```bash
npm install worker-sync-db
```

Peer: TypeScript 5+. React 18+ only if you import `worker-sync-db/react`.

## Quick start

```typescript
import {
  createDatabase,
  defineSchema,
  sharedWorkerUrl,
  dedicatedWorkerUrl,
} from 'worker-sync-db';

const schema = defineSchema({
  todos: { keyPath: 'id', indexes: { byStatus: 'status' } },
});

const db = await createDatabase({
  schema,
  dbName: 'my-app',
  sharedWorker: sharedWorkerUrl,
  dedicatedWorker: dedicatedWorkerUrl,
});

await db.put('todos', { id: '1', title: 'Buy milk', status: 'open' });
db.subscribe('todos', (e) => {
  if (e.type === 'put') console.log(e.doc);
});
```

## Decision vs Dexie

| Need | Prefer |
|------|--------|
| Single-tab IndexedDB CRUD, mature ecosystem | Dexie |
| SharedWorker multi-tab live fan-out + optional BYO sync queue | worker-sync-db |
| Hosted sync cloud | Dexie Cloud / Firebase / etc. (not this lib) |
